thread:
devon: quick sync — we need a consensus on the per-tenant rate policy shape before I land the enforcement PR. primary goals: predictable latency for paid tiers, user-observable quotas in console, and graceful burst handling for apps that do short traffic spikes. thoughts?

elaine: +1. leaning toward separate controls: steady RPM/TPM for long-term fairness, and a small concurrency cap to protect tail latency. bursts should be allowed but capped by a short window (eg 10s).

sam: agree on two-tier controls. token-bucket for burst with refill = burst_tokens per 10s, and a global RPM/TPM for sustained load. open question: where do we enforce? edge gateway (fast) or at the routing layer (aware of dedicated capacity)?

devon: good call. enforce at the gateway for hosted API to drop fast; route decisions still consult org routing policy so we can fallback to cheaper model when throttled. for Dedicated/Private we should emit advisory throttles at the gateway but allow local override controlled by admin.

mia: telemetry needs: per-org rolling 1m/10m/1h token consumption, concurrent-inflight histogram, rejection reason tags (rate_limit, concurrency, fallback). console should show 95p concurrency and a heatmap of burst events so customers can tune.

elaine: proof-of-concept policy snippet (for console and enforcement):
```json
{
  "org_id": "<org>",
  "sustained_tpm": 60000,
  "sustained_rpm": 1000,
  "concurrency_limit": 50,
  "burst": {
    "window_seconds": 10,
    "max_burst_tokens": 200
  },
  "enforcement_point": "gateway",
  "fallback_policy": "route-to-variant"
}
```

sam: that looks good. suggest adding a soft-limit mode for early-warning (log + 429 but allow one-per-minute override) to avoid immediate customer surprise on rollout.

devon: +1 on soft-limit. rollout plan: feature-flagged enforcement (off by default), opt-in for early adopters, then a 2-week monitor with telemetry alerts and safety kill-switch. infra-bot: can you add a deploy check that prevents flag flip without 7d of metrics? @infra-bot

infra-bot: noted. I can block the flag flip if historical telemetry for that org is < 7 days or if the org has > 10k active tokens in the last 24h. will post details in the PR. :gear:

mia: UI note — add "why was my request throttled" tooltip with reason and a link to recommended thresholds + a one-click request to increase quota for enterprise customers. that reduces support load.

elaine: edge case: many small concurrent streaming connections (websocket-style) can blow the concurrency budget but low token rate. we should allow a separate streaming_connection_limit and treat streaming vs single-request concurrency differently.

devon: good catch. add streaming_connection_limit to the schema, default lower. also document that streaming uses a separate billing/instrumentation path.

analytics: I'll wire up dashboards: per-org time series for token rate, token bucket fill, concurrency, stream connections, 429s by reason. will create alert runbooks for spike in 429:rate_limit or concurrency.

sam: final proposal: enforcement layers = (1) edge gateway for hard caps and fast 429s, (2) routing layer for model fallbacks, (3) org-control-plane for console adjustments + soft-limits. rollout feature flag + soft-mode + 7d telemetry gate.

devon: love it. next steps: I'll draft the PR with the policy schema and enforcement points, elaine + mia review the schema/UI copy, analytics + infra will prepare dashboards and deploy checks. tagging owners: @elaine @mia @sam @analytics. thanks everyone — will update thread with PR link. :rocket:
